1.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs.js – this is the React implementation of Tabs where the dropdown trigger (and its state, event handlers, and conditional rendering between <ul> and <select>) is defined. Removing or refactoring this file is required to eliminate the dropdown variant.

2. packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-test.js – these tests cover the dropdown behavior (toggling dropdownHidden, keyboard navigation in narrow mode, etc.). They must be updated or removed to align with the tab-only approach.

3. packages/react/src/components/Tabs/Tabs-story.js – the Storybook examples still exercise the dropdown variant (triggerHref, iconDescription, knobs for narrow mode). The stories need to be updated to remove references to the dropdown and document only the inline tablist.

4. packages/components/src/components/tabs/tabs.js – this is the vanilla JS/web-components variant that also toggles a dropdown menu on narrow screens. It needs the same removal of dropdown logic (_updateMenuState, trigger selectors) to keep tabs always inline.
1.bug_scenario: In the provided screenshots, when the Tabs component is rendered in a narrow container or at small browser widths, it automatically switches from the horizontal tab list into a dropdown menu (a native <select> or listbox) showing only the current tab label and hiding the other tabs behind the dropdown. When the screen is wide, it renders the standard inline tablist again. The design proposal is to remove this “dropdown” variant entirely, so that tabs always remain as a horizontal tablist regardless of available width.
